findings.exact_estimate: Table 4 (PDF p. 7), N = 235 obs across 75 utilities (models a, e, f) and N = 225 obs across 72 utilities (models b, c, d, g, h, i), restricted to O&M cost recovery <= 2.0 with cluster-robust SEs (SE values not printed): Linear O&M cost recovery is positive and significant across all 9 models (Pooled OLS a = 34.62***, b = 36.04***, c = 33.27**, d = 30.43**; Fixed Effects e = 23.63**; Random Effects f = 31.47***, g = 34.02***, h = 28.32***, i = 27.52***), while Squared O&M cost recovery is negative and significant across all 9 models (sign confirmed by prose on p. 6 and Maximum cr formula; printed without minus glyph as 14.20***, 13.58***, 12.79**, 11.91**, 10.67**, 13.81***, 14.31***, 12.32***, and 12.16***, respectively). Turning-point Maximum cr = -b/(2a) is 1.22, 1.33, 1.30, 1.28 in Pooled OLS (a-d), 1.11 in FE (e), and 1.14, 1.19, 1.15, 1.13 in RE (f-i). Evaluated at covariate means in focal RE model h (Fig. 2, PDF p. 8), 3-year coverage change becomes positive above cr ≈ 0.83, peaks at cr = 1.15, decelerates above 1.15, and turns negative in absolute terms above cr = 1.47.

headline_result_summary: Across an unbalanced panel of 75 urban/peri-urban water utilities in 25 Sub-Saharan African countries (1996–2012; N = 225–235 utility-years), utility O&M cost recovery exhibits a statistically significant inverted-U (quadratic) relationship with 3-year growth in household/public-point water coverage across all pooled OLS, fixed-effects, random-effects, and Tobit specifications. Moderate cost recovery up to an estimated turning point of 1.11–1.20 in panel FE/RE models (1.22–1.33 in pooled OLS) increases subsequent water coverage, whereas higher capital-cost-recovery levels (such as standard regulatory benchmarks of 1.3–2.0) reduce coverage gains and—above approximately 1.47 at sample means—lead to absolute declines in water coverage; meanwhile, on-budget public fiscal expenditure for water consistently and significantly increases water coverage growth, whereas ODA has largely null effects in panel random-effects models.
specification_or_coding_pitfalls: 1. NONLINEAR INVERTED-U RELATIONSHIP: Coding only the positive linear term on O&M cost recovery (+23.63** to +36.04***) as uniformly 'favorable to access' would misrepresent the paper's core thesis and empirical finding, which pairs that linear term with a significant negative quadratic term (-10.67** to -14.31***) showing that high cost-recovery targets (>1.11–1.20, and absolute coverage losses >1.47) harm water coverage expansion. Conversely, unrestricted linear models keeping ~20 outlier observations with cr > 2.0 yield a negative linear slope (Note 13, p. 10), and the unadjusted bivariate correlation is null (0.07, Table 6). 2. STRIPPED UNICODE MINUS SIGNS IN PDF TEXT EXTRACTION: Every negative sign (U+2212) in the extracted tables and equations (Tables 4, 5, 6, 8, 9; Eq. 3) was dropped by the PDF text layer (e.g., Initial water coverage, Squared O&M cost recovery, Non Revenue Water, and Min coverage change -81 appear without '-' signs). For all main variables, exact signs are explicitly confirmed by the prose text (pp. 6–8) and the reported turning points Maximum cr = -b/(2a) (e.g., 28.32 / (2 * 12.32) = 1.15 in model h); however, for control dummies never discussed directionally in prose (such as National utility = 12.85** in Table 9 model h4), the sign should not be guessed. 3. INVERTED SIGNIFICANCE-STAR FOOTNOTE IN TABLE 4: The note to Table 4 (p. 7) prints '*, ** and *** stand for 1%, 5%, and 10% significance level, respectively'—a typographical reversal by the authors; the prose (pp. 6–7) and F/chi-squared statistics confirm standard convention where *** = 1% ('strongly significant') and * = 10% ('only marginally significant' for ODA = 3.61*). 4. OUTCOME DEFINITION: Water coverage follows IBNET/MDG binary access within the utility's service area (combining direct household piped connections and public water points) and does not separate household connections from public taps or measure supply continuity/affordability directly.
study_design: Observational unbalanced utility-level panel econometric study using lagged explanatory variables (3-year forward change in water coverage from t to t+3 regressed on covariates at t) estimated via Pooled OLS, Utility Fixed Effects, Random Effects, and Random-Effects Panel Tobit (1996–2009 base years with outcomes through 2012).
unit_and_sample_size: Urban and peri-urban water utilities in Sub-Saharan Africa: N = 235 utility-year observations across 75 utilities (25 countries) in models without public expenditure (Table 4 models a, e, f), and N = 225 utility-year observations across 72 utilities (22 countries) in models including public expenditure (Table 4 models b, c, d, g, h, i), restricted to O&M cost recovery <= 2.0 (robustness samples: N = 234 and N = 224 in Tobit outlier models [Table 8]; N = 221 across 69 utilities excluding 3 South African District Municipalities [Table 9 model h5]; nearly half of utilities are in Nigeria [18 utilities, 34 obs], Zambia [10 utilities, 75 obs], and South Africa [8 utilities, 20 obs]).
